title: config/parity.json
description: The language-parity declaration, read by scripts/kit/parity.mts: the implementations of the repository (the one source of the language set) and the units that every implementation must hold. The facts come from the tree: the checker runs the bindings and the symbol extractors and reads the error-code artifacts. Every path lies inside the repository (S3): none is absolute, starts with ~ or holds a .. segment, in a path field or in a word (between =, : and whitespace) of a runner argument, env value or binding command, and no env sets PYTHONPATH; a package is tested as installed.

name.description: The name of the implementation, used by the bindings and documents.

prose.description: The names that the documents write for the implementation besides its name, such as "PHP extension" for php-extension; R10 reads each, in any case, as the implementation. A prose name is a name of no other implementation and is declared once.

runner.description: How a binding runs and reads its outcomes, through the output parsers of scripts/kit/test-output.mts: go (go test -json), cargo (cargo test), node (node --test with the reporter scripts/kit/parity-node-reporter.mts), vitest (node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run with the JSON reporter of vitest), php (PHPUnit of the Composer package of the test, TeamCity messages) and python (the python3 of mise.toml, var/tools/mise/shims/python3, -m unittest -v). A case is a subtest, a test named by the case, or a test method test_<case>.

roots.description: The directories that hold the implementation and its tests; the whole repository is no root.

tests.description: Globs of test files of the implementation that the convention of its runner does not select; they add to its test files and never remove one. The test files of an implementation are the files in its roots that the convention of its runner selects (scripts/kit/parity-declaration.mts CONVENTIONS: go **/*_test.go; cargo **/tests/**/*.rs and every .rs file with a test attribute; node **/*.test.{ts,mts,cts,mjs,cjs,js}; vitest **/*.{test,spec}.{ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs,tsx,jsx}; php **/*Test.php; python **/test_*.py) and the files of these globs. Each one, except a file of its support globs, must be the test of a binding, and so must a file in its roots that is named like a test (*_test.*, test_*.*, *Test.*, *.test.*, *.spec.*).

support.description: Globs of the test-support files of the implementation: files in its roots that its tests or the testPatterns of its runner select but that hold no test, such as a Go helper that must end in _test.go. A support file is no test of a binding; a Go support file declares no function that go test runs, a cargo support file holds no test attribute, and parity-check runs each node, php and python support file once and fails when it reports a case. Each glob selects at least one such file.

command.description: The program of the runner: a path relative to the root of the checkout when it holds a /, else a name on PATH. Default: go, cargo, the running node, php, var/tools/mise/shims/python3. ${NAME} is the value of NAME in the invoking environment when the bindings run.

args.description: Arguments of the program: after test for go and cargo; before the test file for node, before the PHPUnit path for php (the run of php then names the configuration of its package with --configuration <package>/phpunit.xml or phpunit.xml.dist, or --no-configuration when it has neither) and before -m unittest for python. ${NAME} is the value of NAME in the invoking environment when the bindings run.

env.description: Variables set for the runs of this implementation only, over the environment of the check. ${NAME} in a value is the value of NAME in the invoking environment when the bindings run; an unset or empty NAME is a finding of the runs of the implementation, and there is no default form.

symbols.description: The public API of the implementation, which parity-check reads with the extractor of its ecosystem (scripts/kit/parity-symbols.mts): go (golang.org/x/tools/go/packages on a module directory, built by install-tools when config/toolchain.json symbolExtractors names go), php (nikic/php-parser on a source directory or file, such as the *.stub.php of an extension, installed when symbolExtractors names php), python (the standard library's ast on a package directory or module file), rust (the rustdoc JSON of the library of a Cargo.toml, with the Rust nightly of config/toolchain.json exceptions whose scope holds it) or ts (API Extractor on a .d.ts entry point in its npm package).

entry.description: The path that the extractor reads, relative to the checkout.

errors.description: The generated error-code artifact of the implementation and the regular expression whose first group is a code.

shares.description: The implementation whose test files this one runs in its own runtime, such as a native extension that runs the tests of the library it replaces. R6 accepts a binding test of this implementation in the roots of the shared one; R5 still judges only this implementation's own roots and tests. It names another implementation of the same runner (K232).

suites.description: Globs of the shared vector files; each one must be the file of a suite unit.

tools.description: The directories of single-language tooling tests that implement no contract, such as the tests of an editor tool; every run prints each with its reason. R6 accepts a test there, and R3 and R5 do not judge it. A root overlaps no implementation root and holds no test of a binding.

reason.description: Why the tests of the root belong to no implementation.

comparators.description: The directories of the checks that compare the outputs of several implementations; a test there belongs to no implementation.

testPatterns.description: Globs of test files of a runner across the repository that its convention does not select; they add to the convention and never remove a file. Such a file lies in a root of an implementation of that runner or in a comparator root.

requirements.description: The requirement ids of the spec (K273): docs/spec/**/*.md, not the Korean twins, defines each as a bullet **<id>** or a heading <id> whose id matches pattern.

pattern.description: A regular expression of one id, without anchors, such as HY-[0-9]+.

id.description: The name of the unit; the findings name a case of a suite as <id>/<case>.

kind.description: suite: the shared cases of a vector file, run by a binding of each implementation; feature: one native test of each implementation, named by its id; api: an exported symbol of each implementation.

requirements.description: The ids of the spec requirements that the unit tests (K273): each is defined in docs/spec as a bullet **<id>** or a heading <id>; every requirement is cited by a unit (R13), and a unit cites only defined ones (R14).

file.description: suite: the vector file, or the directory whose case directories cases selects.

cases.description: suite: for a vector file, the path of the case names in the file, $ followed by .<key> and [*] steps and ending with an optional .~ step that selects the keys of an object as the names; for a directory, a glob relative to it whose / steps each match one directory level and whose matches are the case directories, each named by its path relative to the directory (*/* over <group>/<case>/), whose case.json lists in requirements the ids that the case tests (K277). A file that the glob matches is a declaration finding.

caseFile.description: suite whose file is a directory: the file name that a case directory holds to be a case of this unit, so units that share one directory each take the cases that hold the output they compare (K277).

bindings.description: suite and feature: the native test of each implementation.

command.description: The repository command that runs the binding in place of the default runner of its implementation: an argv array, its first word the program (a path relative to the root of the checkout when it holds a /, else a name on PATH) and the others its arguments, run in the directory of the implementation that holds the test (the root of roots that holds it). The runner reads the output of the command as it reads that of its default, so the command must print what the runner reads (go test -json, cargo test, node --test, vitest's JSON report, PHPUnit TeamCity, unittest); a command is used as declared, with no fallback to the default when it cannot start or fails. ${NAME} in a word is the value of NAME in the invoking environment when the bindings run, resolved as the references of command, args and env are; an unset or empty NAME is a finding of the runs of this binding, which then run nothing, and there is no default form.

symbol.description: suite, go: the test function whose subtests are the cases; cargo: the module path whose tests <symbol>::<case> are the cases; php (optional): the test method <class>::<method> of a fully qualified class, which runs alone (--filter) and whose data sets `<method> with data set "<case>"` are the cases; without it, the test methods test_<case> of the file are the cases.

id.description: feature: the id of the test as its runner reports it in a run of the whole test file, which must pass in both runs: go the test or subtest name (TestX/case), cargo the libtest path (module::test), node and vitest the names of the test and its enclosing suites joined by ' › ', php and python the test method.

symbols.description: api: the symbol id of each implementation, as its symbol extractor gives it.

errors.description: The error-code catalog that every implementation generates.

catalog.description: The catalog file and the regular expression whose first group is a code.

languageLists.description: Lists of implementation names in other files, each equal to the set of the implementations.

pattern.description: A regular expression whose first group holds the list; its words are the names.

documents.description: The documents whose counts and lists of implementations must match the implementations.

nouns.description: The words that a count of implementations precedes, such as languages or 언어.
